title: Blue Notebook Review - Sgt. Verbeck Addresses 75% Increase in Arrests
description:
Sgt. Rick is back with this week’s Blue Notebook Review, answering questions from last week and taking a closer look at the reported 75% increase in arrests.

This week’s update covers arrests, the recovery of over 90 stolen items, traffic enforcement, homelessness engagement, and a few grand openings around the city.

Watch the full review and stay informed on what’s happening in Santa Monica.
transcript_text: Hello, Santa Monica. My name is Sergeant Rick and this is a UBN update review. During last week's video, we're on the pier celebrating the 100-year anniversary of Route 66 in which the fire department versus the police department were challenged to eat a 72-oz steak and we won. Again, uh I had made a comment that our arrests were up 75% and one of the viewers had essentially asked, "Why is it up 75%? Like what changed?" So, there's not just one thing that I can I can pinpoint. It It's probably a collection of 10 different things. One, we have a new uh city manager, Oliver Chi. We have a new chief of police, Derek Jacob. We're working closely together to implement the realignment plan. We were authorized to hire more officers, so now we can more efficiently put the cops on the dots. We were given a grant to build our smart center, which has paid dividends in catching those looking to do harm to our residents, visitors, and businesses. We have a new district attorney, uh Nathan Hochman, who's all about filing those those felony cases. Our own city attorneys, led by Janet Grisby, and I think she mentioned that their filings are up 300%. We have our men and women in blue on the streets working long hours. I mean, working their butts off, working overtime, uh being forced hired to work during holidays and special events. And then we have our our specialized units, like our crime impact team, our help team, our other than our specialized unit, but our detectives, and our downtown services unit. All that together, working together, has led to that 75% increase in arrests. And our self-initiated activity is up 49%. So, being proactive, not just waiting on the radio calls. All that combined is why I think our arrests are up 25%. Although the haters will just say that we're corrupt and we don't do anything anyways, but the numbers speak for themselves. So, enough about me. Hopefully, that answers your question. Uh why don't we hear from the NROs to talk about the crime and our efforts to combat that crime during last reporting period. And since we're talking about crime, why don't we have Officer Hollowell, your Beat 1 NRO, start us off. So, Hollowell, kick us off. >> Thanks, Sergeant Rick. Officer Steven Hollowell here, your Beat 1 Neighborhood Resource Officer for the Pier, the Beach, and the Promenade. And for this operational period, for crime suppression, officers responded to 2,593 calls for service, as well as conducted 93 arrests. And for the incidents of note, Santa Monica police officers responded to 500 Wilshire, CVS, for theft call, and located one suspect. Upon further investigation, they had located two additional suspects in the vehicle in the parking lot, where they recovered 90 other stolen items. >> Bing bong. >> Great job, Santa Monica police. Way to put in the work. Hey, bad guys, you might want to think twice before coming to Santa Monica. And for the second incident of note, Santa Monica police officers were in the area of Appian Way conducting patrol, when they located four suspects within a vehicle with open containers, marijuana, and nitrous How do you say? Nitrous oxide? Upon further investigation, they inventory the vehicle and discovered that the vehicle contained one Glock pistol. Hey, bad guy, you're not supposed to have that. They went straight to jail. Maybe not all of them, but at least some of them. And thank you. Back to you in the studio, Sergeant Rick. >> Thanks, Hollowell. And great work by our troops finding over 90 other stolen items. That's really good. And let's keep the momentum going. And let's hear from our B2 in a row officer Pardo to talk about our traffic enforcement efforts. Izzy, what do you got? >> Hey Santa Monica, B2 neighborhood resource officer Pardo here with your traffic update for the week. This week our traffic team conducted 297 traffic stops and issued 191 citations. Great job. So yes, we were once outside again. Outside and making eye contact with your Vic lights. We also had a felony hit-and-run collision near 1900 Cloverfield where a pedestrian was struck while unlawfully crossing the street. That wasn't good. The driver left the scene but was later located and arrested for felony hit-and-run. Thankfully, the pedestrian's injuries were non-life-threatening. And on May 27th, officers conducted a citywide motorcycle safety enforcement operation reminding everyone that whether you are on two wheels or four, traffic laws still apply to everyone. Safety tip, use marked crosswalks, stay visible, and drivers, please remain at the scene at any collision. Leaving only makes a bad situation much worse. And this is the type of crosswalk I'm talking about. Use it. That's all I got. Back to you in the studio, Sarge. >> Thanks, Izzy. In regards to traffic collisions since you're talking about it, uh I also want to point out that if you're involved in a minor traffic collision, when safe, pull over to the side of the road so you're out of traffic. Um a lot of people, if they're in a minor fender bender, just keep the cars right where they are. We don't need that for the police report. So, move it over safely, get out of traffic. God forbid, I don't want another accident to be caused because of your accident. And it's just not it's not safe to be out there in the number one or number two lane traffic. So, pull over, exchange information, if there's a problem, give us a call. And let's keep it moving. And let's hear from let's say your Beat 3 NRO, Officer Tago. Who, by the way, joined our Chief of Police during the steak eating contest. Obviously came out victorious. Uh and he's going to talk about our efforts with the homeless population. So, Tago, what do you got? >> Aloha, Officer Tago here, your Beat 3 Neighborhood Resource Officer. And here are your health team stats for this past reporting period. The health team responded to 38 radio calls, conducted 202 self-initiated contacts, made 18 arrests, issued 35 citations, and addressed seven encampments. And here's your incident of note. Officers responded to an encampment in a children's play area at Tongva Park. Upon arrival, officers located two individuals living inside a tent that had been set up within one of the park's play structures. During the investigation, officers discovered one of the subjects had a $100,000 Santa Monica Police Department warrant related to dangerous drugs, and he was ultimately taken to jail. Children should be playing in our parks, not sharing them with criminal activity. Back to the studio, Sarge. >> Thanks, Tago. And health team, thank you for keeping our parks safe for our families. We really do appreciate it. And last but not least, let's hear from your Beat 4 NRO, Officer Villa, to talk to you about our community engagement efforts. Brandon, what do you got? >> Hello, Blue Notebook family. I'm here at the grand opening of The Window, located in the 900 block of Montana. Speaking of grand openings, SMPD had our grand opening of the downtown substation during this reporting period. Your community engagement team also met with neighborhood and business groups. We also had school tours at our station with our youth groups. Well, that's all I have for this week. It's pretty short and sweet. So, I want to go get a burger. We'll see you soon. >> Brandon, can you get me one, too? I'm starving over here. Brandon? Did Brandon already leave? I swear, that guy never gets me anything. Well, that, my friends, concludes this week's Blue Note Book Review. Remember, we have one shot at this thing called life. Spend it doing something positive. Spend it with a loved one, with with friends, with enjoying nature, with improving someone else's life. Don't spend it with negative thoughts or or just some hate in your heart. It's not worth it. You have one shot at this. Trust me. When it's the last few minutes of your life, you're going to wish you spent more time with your loved ones. Not more time sending angry comments to random YouTube channels. Until next week. >> parking lot and recovered 90 additional personal hot dog.
